newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean yields end down on falling new issues.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean yields end down on falling new issues.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds ended lower as investment trust companies actively bought on belief that next month's issues would shrink for the second straight month.

Dealers said some financial institutions were reluctant to guarantee many corporate bonds following the Kia Group's financial troubles that touched off rumours some other conglomerates also faced similar problems. This resulted in fewer new issues.
* 3-yr corporates closed down at 11.80 pct vs 11.90 pct
* 3-mth CDs closed down at 11.90 pct vs 12.00 pct
* Overnight average call rate at 12.08 pct vs 11.84 pct
"Financial institutions have been reluctant to guarantee bonds since Kia's financial problems, making newer issues smaller and smaller," said Kang Yung-gee at Hyundai Securities.
He said yields were likely to end little changed in thin trading on Tuesday as only a small portion of planned issues was guaranteed by financial institutions.
